name: Two Individually Ineffective Ample Additions Can Cooperatively Restore a Root
statement: There is a 870-concept rooted factor $S$ with two adjacent ample additions $u,v$ such that both one-concept extensions remain rooted factors, while $S\cup\{u,v\}$ peels to the original root. The two additions have the same initial acquired support of size four; after either is present, adding the other acquires a support of size five.
proof: The partially replicated-tip theorem evaluates singleton occurrence rows as rooted factors and either incident edge row as root-positive exactly when the underlying third tip repairs the base root. The certified tip $604$ has such a root-ending order, so its two singleton copies are individually ineffective while their edge row restores the endpoint. Direct replay verifies all eight occurrence rows and every proper rooted minor.
